Hope at [Lackland Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lackland_Air_Force_Base "Lackland Air Force Base") in Texas in 1990

Along with his best friend Bing Crosby, Hope was offered a commission in the United States Navy as lieutenant commander during World War II, but [FDR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FDR "FDR") intervened, believing it would be better for troop morale if they kept doing what they were doing by playing for _all_ branches of military service.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHope1990119-77)

For his service to his nation through the USO, he was awarded the [Sylvanus Thayer Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvanus_Thayer_Award "Sylvanus Thayer Award") by the [United States Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy") at West Point in 1968, the first entertainer to receive the award.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Thayer_award-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-79) A 1997 act of [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") signed by President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") named Hope an "Honorary Veteran". He remarked, "I've been given many awards in my lifetime, but to be numbered among the men and women I admire most is the greatest honor I have ever received."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFaith2003429-80) In an homage to Hope, comedian/TV host [Stephen Colbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Colbert "Stephen Colbert") carried a golf club on stage during the week of USO performances he taped for his TV show _[The Colbert Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Colbert\_Report "The Colbert Report")_ during the 2009 season.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-LA_Times_June_2009-81)

_Dear Bob...: Bob Hope's Wartime Correspondence with the G.I.s of World War II,_ written by Martha Bolton (first woman staff writer for Bob Hope) and Linda Hope (his elder daughter), is a collection of some of his letter to the troops.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-82)

### Sports car racing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Sports car racing")]

During a short stint in 1960, Hope became a part owner of the [Riverside International Raceway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_International_Raceway "Riverside International Raceway") in [Moreno Valley, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moreno_Valley,_California "Moreno Valley, California"), along with [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") co-owner Fred Levy Jr.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-83) and oil tycoon Ed Pauley for $800,000 (adjusted to $7.0 million in 2020). [Les Richter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Richter "Les Richter") was made president of the raceway.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-84)

### Land development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Land development")]

Hope owned thousands of acres of Southern Caliornia, and was involved in numerous land developments.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-group_1990_12_09_latimes-85)

He settled in [Palm Springs, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs,_California "Palm Springs, California"), in 1946, and began to acquire and develop land throughout the area. In 1948, he was named "Honorary Mayor" of the community.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-palmspringslife_2017-12-29-86)

He also owned an East Coast race track. the "Atlantic City Race Course," with [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra") and others, at its start in 1946.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-vista-87)

## Influence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Influence")]

In an interview on [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR"), [Terry Gross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Gross "Terry Gross") said, "[Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen") and [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") are two of the people who have referred to Bob Hope as influences. And I think influences in part on their own personas as not being this suave, handsome, macho guy." Hope biographer Zoglin agreed saying, "Woody continually said, this was the guy who influenced me more than anyone else. And that character - that kind of scared character, the guy talk - nervous, talking his way through, you know, bad times and scary times. That was Woody Allen's character in _[Sleeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper\_(1973\_film) "Sleeper (1973 film)")_ (1973) and _[Love and Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_and\_Death "Love and Death")_ (1975). He always said that he and [Diane Keaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Keaton "Diane Keaton") in those films were basically like Hope and [Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby")".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-88)

[Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") also cited Hope as an influence saying, "I loved Woody Allen. And Woody Allen says, oh, I love Bob Hope, he really influenced me. And I thought, what are you talking about? How did Bob Hope influence you in any way?...Then I went back and I started looking at seeing some of the movies. And you see it, you see that that the character that Woody Allen does is a character that I think was really, to a large extent invented by Bob Hope."[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-89)

## Artistry and legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Artistry and legacy")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Cat-and-the-Canary-1939.jpg/250px-Cat-and-the-Canary-1939.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cat-and-the-Canary-1939.jpg)

[Douglass Montgomery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglass_Montgomery "Douglass Montgomery"), Bob Hope, [Paulette Goddard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulette_Goddard "Paulette Goddard") and [John Beal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Beal_(actor) "John Beal (actor)") in _[The Cat and the Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cat\_and\_the\_Canary\_(1939\_film) "The Cat and the Canary (1939 film)")_ (1939)

Hope helped establish modern American comedy.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-PBS-22) He was widely praised for his comedic timing and his specialization in the use of [one-liners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-liner_joke "One-liner joke") and rapid-fire delivery of jokes. He was known for his style of self-deprecating jokes, first building himself up and then tearing himself down. He performed hundreds of times per year.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998158-90) Such early films as _[The Cat and the Canary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cat\_and\_the\_Canary\_(1939\_film) "The Cat and the Canary (1939 film)")_ (1939) and _[The Paleface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Paleface\_(1948\_film) "The Paleface (1948 film)")_ (1948) were financially successful and praised by critics,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998123,_183-91) and by the mid-1940s, with his radio program getting good ratings as well, he was one of the most popular entertainers in the United States.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998153-92) When Paramount threatened to stop production of the "Road" pictures in 1945, they received 75,000 letters of protest.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998172-93)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Jerry_colonna_bob_hope_1940_nbc.JPG/250px-Jerry_colonna_bob_hope_1940_nbc.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jerry_colonna_bob_hope_1940_nbc.JPG)

Hope and his comic sidekick, [Jerry Colonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Colonna_(entertainer) "Jerry Colonna (entertainer)"), sporting his trademark handlebar mustache in 1940

Hope had no faith in his skills as a dramatic actor, and his performances of that type were not as well received.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998184,_187-94) He had been well known in radio until the late 1940s; however, as his ratings began to slip in the 1950s, he switched to television and became an early pioneer of that medium.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002160-51)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998173-95) He published several books, notably dictating to [ghostwriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghostwriter "Ghostwriter") about his wartime experiences.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998153-92)

Although Hope made an effort to keep his material up to date, he never adapted his comic persona or his routines to any great degree. As Hollywood began to transition to the "[New Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hollywood "New Hollywood")" era in the 1960s, he reacted negatively, such as when he hosted the [40th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40th_Academy_Awards "40th Academy Awards") in 1968 and voiced his contempt by mocking the show's delay because of the assassination of [Martin Luther King Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr. "Martin Luther King Jr.") and condescendingly greeted attending younger actors on stage—such as [Dustin Hoffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dustin_Hoffman "Dustin Hoffman"), who was 30 at the time—as children.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-96) By the 1970s, his popularity was beginning to wane with military personnel and with the movie-going public in general.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998255,_276,_314-97) However, he continued doing USO tours into the 1980s[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002161-98) and continued to appear on television into the 1990s. Former First Lady [Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan"), a close friend and frequent host to him at the White House, called Hope "America's most honored citizen and our favorite clown".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998312-99)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Bob_Hope_playing_golf_in_the_Oval_Office.png/250px-Bob_Hope_playing_golf_in_the_Oval_Office.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_playing_golf_in_the_Oval_Office.png)

Hope, a golf fan, putting a golf ball into an ashtray held by President [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") in the [Oval Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office") in 1973

Hope was well known as an avid golfer, playing in as many as 150 charity tournaments a year.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens200257-100) Introduced to the game in the 1930s while performing in [Winnipeg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winnipeg "Winnipeg"), Canada,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Manitoba_Historic_Society_1988-101) he eventually played to a four [handicap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_handicap "Golf handicap"). His love for the game—and the humor he could find in it—made him a sought-after [foursome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foursome_(golf) "Foursome (golf)") member. He once remarked that President [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower") gave up golf for painting: "Fewer strokes, you know."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-panews_May_1980-102) He also was quoted as saying, "It's wonderful how you can start out with three strangers in the morning, play 18 holes, and by the time the day is over you have three solid enemies."[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Golf_Hall_of_Fame-103)

A golf club became an integral [prop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prop "Prop") for Hope during the standup segments of his television specials and USO shows. In 1978 he putted against the then-two-year-old [Tiger Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Woods "Tiger Woods") in a television appearance with the actor [Jimmy Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Stewart "Jimmy Stewart") on _[The Mike Douglas Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mike\_Douglas\_Show "The Mike Douglas Show")_.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Fox_Sports_2012-104)

The [Bob Hope Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Classic "Bob Hope Classic"), founded in 1960, made history in 1995 when Hope teed up for the opening round in a foursome that included presidents [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford"), [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), and [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"), the only time three U.S. presidents played in the same golf foursome.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-bhcc_History-105) The event, now known as the CareerBuilder Challenge, was one of the few [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour "PGA Tour") tournaments that took place over five rounds, until the 2012 tournament when it was cut back to the conventional four.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Business_Wire-106)

Hope had a heavy interest in sports beyond golf and his brief fling as a professional boxer in his youth. In 1946, he bought a small stake in the [Cleveland Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Indians "Cleveland Indians") professional baseball team[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Windsor_Star_1946-107) and held it for most of the rest of his life.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Rea_1982-108) He appeared on the June 3, 1963, cover of _[Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ magazine wearing an Indians uniform,[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sports_Illustrated_cover-109) and sang a special version of "Thanks for the Memories" after the Indians' last game at [Cleveland Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Stadium "Cleveland Stadium") on October 3, 1993.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Dawidziak_2003-110) He also bought a share with Bing Crosby of the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") football team in 1947, but sold it in 1962.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Lodi_News_1962-111) He frequently used his television specials to promote the annual [AP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press")[College Football All-America Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Football_All-America_Team "College Football All-America Team"). The players would come onstage one by one and introduce themselves, then Hope, often dressed in a football uniform, would give a one-liner about the player or his school.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FWAA_2009-112)

## Acting credits and accolades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Acting credits and accolades")]

Main articles: [Bob Hope filmography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_filmography "Bob Hope filmography") and [List of awards and nominations received by Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Bob_Hope "List of awards and nominations received by Bob Hope")

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_gets_plaque_on_Hill.jpg)

Hope and his wife Dolores on [Capitol Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Hill "Capitol Hill") as he received an award in 1978

Hope was awarded more than 2,000 honors and awards, including 54 honorary university doctorates. In 1963 President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") awarded him the [Congressional Gold Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Gold_Medal "Congressional Gold Medal") for service to his country.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002152%E2%80%93153-113) President [Lyndon Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Johnson "Lyndon Johnson") bestowed the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom") in 1969 for his service to the armed forces through the [USO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USO "USO").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-usa-patriotism.com-114) In 1982 he received the S. Roger Horchow Award for Greatest Public Service by a Private Citizen, an honor given annually by [Jefferson Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Awards "Jefferson Awards").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Horchow_Award-115) He was presented with the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts") in 1995[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-National_Medal_of_Arts-116) and received the [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award") in 1997.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Times_Union_1997-117) On June 10, 1980, he became the 64th—and only civilian—recipient of the United States Air Force [Order of the Sword](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Sword_(United_States) "Order of the Sword (United States)") which recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to the enlisted corps.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Air_University-118)

Several buildings and facilities were renamed for Hope, including the historic [Fox California Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Theater_(Stockton,_California)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fox Theater (Stockton, California) (page does not exist)") in downtown [Stockton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockton,_California "Stockton, California"),[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Mohawk_Group-119) and the [Bob Hope Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Airport "Bob Hope Airport") in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Daily_News_2010-120) There is a Bob Hope Gallery at the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-121) In memory of his mother, Avis Townes Hope, Bob and Dolores Hope gave the [Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_National_Shrine_of_the_Immaculate_Conception "Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception") in Washington, D.C., a chapel called the Chapel of [Our Lady of Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Hope "Our Lady of Hope").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-122)[USNS _Bob Hope_(T-AKR-300)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Bob_Hope "MV Bob Hope") of the U.S. [Military Sealift Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Sealift_Command "Military Sealift Command") was named for the performer in 1997. It is one of very few [U.S. naval ships that were named after living people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._military_vessels_named_after_living_Americans "List of U.S. military vessels named after living Americans").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FAS_2011-123) The Air Force named a [C-17 Globemaster III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III "C-17 Globemaster III") transport aircraft the _Spirit of Bob Hope_.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Warplanes_Online_Community-124)

In 1965, he was awarded an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters (L.H.D.) degree from [Whittier College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_College "Whittier College").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-125)

In 1978, Hope was invited to [dot the "i"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band#Script_Ohio_and_dotting_the_%22i%22 "Ohio State University Marching Band") in the [Ohio State University Marching Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band "Ohio State University Marching Band")'s "Script Ohio" formation, an honor only given to non-band members on 14 occasions from 1936 through 2016.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-126)[Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen") wrote and narrated a documentary honoring him, _My Favorite Comedian_, shown at [Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center "Lincoln Center").[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-127) In Hope's hometown of Cleveland, the refurbished [Lorain-Carnegie Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorain-Carnegie_Bridge "Lorain-Carnegie Bridge") was renamed the Hope Memorial Bridge in 1983, though differing claims have been made as to whether the bridge honors Hope himself, his entire family, or his stonemason father who helped in the bridge's construction. Also, East 14th Street near [Playhouse Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playhouse_Square "Playhouse Square") in Cleveland's theater district was renamed Memory Lane-Bob Hope Way in 2003 in honor of the entertainer's 100th birthday.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-128)

In 1992, Hope was honored with the "Lombardi Award of Excellence" from the Vince Lombardi Cancer Foundation. The award was created to honor the football coach's legacy, and is awarded annually to an individual who exemplifies his spirit. He was also inducted into [Omicron Delta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa"), the National Leadership Honor Society, in 1992 at [Ferris State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris_State_University "Ferris State University"). On May 28, 2003, President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") established the [Bob Hope American Patriot Award](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2013306 "s:Executive Order 13306").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-129)

*   [25th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25th_Academy_Awards "25th Academy Awards") (1952): Honorary Award for his contribution to the laughter of the world, his service to the motion picture industry, and his devotion to the American premise

*   [38th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/38th_Academy_Awards "38th Academy Awards") (1965): Honorary Award: first Academy Gold Medal for unique and distinguished service to the industry and the academy

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Marriage and relationships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Marriage and relationships")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope%2C_North_Hollywood%2C_California_A.jpg/250px-1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope%2C_North_Hollywood%2C_California_A.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope,_North_Hollywood,_California_A.jpg)

Residence of Bob Hope, North Hollywood, California

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg)

The Hope family; Back, from left: Tony, Dolores, and Linda; Front, from left: Kelly, Bob, and Nora

Hope was briefly married to vaudeville partner Grace Louise Troxell (1912–1992), a secretary from Chicago, Illinois. They were married on January 25, 1933, in Erie, Pennsylvania.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199866-131) They divorced in November 1934.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sheridan_2014-132)

The couple had shared headliner status with Joe Howard at the Palace Theatre in April 1931, performing "Keep Smiling" and the "Antics of 1931".[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-133) They worked together at the RKO Albee, performing the "Antics of 1933" along with Ann Gillens and Johnny Peters in June of that year.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-134) The following month, singer [Dolores Reade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Reade "Dolores Reade") joined Hope's vaudeville troupe and was performing with him at Loew's Metropolitan Theater. She was described as a "former [Ziegfeld beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziegfeld_girl "Ziegfeld girl") and one of society's favorite nightclub entertainers, having appeared at many private social functions at New York, Palm Beach, and Southampton".[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-135)

His marriage to Reade was fraught with ambiguities. As [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") wrote in his 2014 biography _Hope: Entertainer of the Century_,

> Bob and Dolores always claimed that they married in February 1934 in Erie, Pennsylvania. But at that time, he was secretly married to his vaudeville partner Louise Troxell, after three years together on and off. I found divorce papers for Bob and Louise dated November 1934, so either Bob Hope was a bigamist, or he lied about marrying Dolores in February that year. He had actually married Louise in January 1933 in Erie when they were traveling on the vaudeville circuit. When he claimed he had married Dolores in Erie he was miles away in New York, on Broadway. More intriguing, there is no record anywhere of his marriage to Dolores, if it happened. And there are no wedding photos, either. But he never forgot Louise and quietly sent her money in her later years.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sheridan_2014-132)

Dolores had been one of Hope's co-stars on Broadway in _Roberta_. The couple adopted four children: Linda (in 1939), Anthony "Tony" (1940–2004),[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-136) Kelly (1946), and Eleanora "Nora" (1946).[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199886%E2%80%9387-137) Bob and Dolores were also the legal guardians of Tracey, the youngest daughter of famous New York City bar owner [Bernard "Toots" Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_Shor "Toots Shor") and his wife, Marion "Baby" Shor.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-138) In 1935, the couple lived in Manhattan. In 1937, they moved to 10346 Moorpark Street in the [Toluca Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake "Toluca Lake") neighborhood of Los Angeles, where they would reside until their respective deaths.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-140)

Hope had a reputation as a womanizer and continued to see other women throughout his marriage.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199882,_90-141) Zoglin wrote that Hope had several "affairs with chorus girls, beauty queens, singers and showbiz wannabes". Women who have claimed to have been romantically linked to Hope include [Barbara Payton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Payton "Barbara Payton"), [Marilyn Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Maxwell "Marilyn Maxwell"), and [Rosemarie Frankland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemarie_Frankland "Rosemarie Frankland").[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd200665-142)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd200666,_67-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006311-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006313-145)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006313-145)[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Arthur_Marx_1993-146)

### Politics and beliefs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Politics and beliefs")]

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg/250px-Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg)

From left to right: [Spiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiro_Agnew "Spiro Agnew") and [Judy Agnew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Agnew "Judy Agnew"), Bob and [Dolores Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Hope "Dolores Hope"), [Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") and [Pat Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Nixon "Pat Nixon"), [Nancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") and [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") during a campaign stop for the [Nixon-Agnew ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon-Agnew_ticket "Nixon-Agnew ticket") in California, 1971

Hope had extensive relationships with US Presidents from [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt") to [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") and often made topical political jokes in his comedic material. He hosted the [White House Correspondents Dinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Correspondents_Dinner "White House Correspondents Dinner") three times in 1944, 1953, and 1976.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-147)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-148)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-ford-149) Hope was supportive politically of [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") Presidents such as [Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") and [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-150)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-151)

Hope's biographer [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") in an interview with [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR") stated that "Bob Hope was the establishment. Bob Hope was friends with [Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon "Nixon"). Bob Hope was speaking in favor of the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"). Bob Hope was expressing that kind of backward, suburban, [WASP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WASP "WASP") view of minorities, [homosexuals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homosexuals "Homosexuals"), the [women's movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_movement "Women's movement")."[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-152) Hope's beliefs and attitudes on social issues are a part of the plot of the 2020 film _[Misbehaviour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misbehaviour\_(film) "Misbehaviour (film)")_, which follows the [Women's Liberation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_Liberation "Women's Liberation") protests at the [Miss World 1970](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_World_1970 "Miss World 1970") competition that Hope hosted; [Greg Kinnear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Kinnear "Greg Kinnear") plays Hope.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-153)

[![Image 31](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/President_Ronald_Reagan_and_Nancy_Reagan_Talking_with_Bob_Hope_During_The_State_Dinner_for_Prime_Minister_Thatcher_at_The_White_House_-_DPLA_-_2db8a4b53ef061b70538102c33453b61.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Ronald_Reagan_and_Nancy_Reagan_Talking_with_Bob_Hope_During_The_State_Dinner_for_Prime_Minister_Thatcher_at_The_White_House_-_DPLA_-_2db8a4b53ef061b70538102c33453b61.jpg)

Hope (left) with [Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") and President [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") in 1981

After the shootings of president Ronald Reagan and [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") in 1981, Hope advocated for [gun control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control "Gun control"). Hope told [Tom Shales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shales "Tom Shales") of _The Washington Post_, "I'm for gun registration. I don't think any jerk that's coked up or anything should be allowed to walk in a store and buy a gun and turn around and shoot 19 people, you know? ... And what the hell, hunters can have their guns, they're registered. I've got a gun in each house for a warning thing; that can be registered ... They gotta tell me what's wrong with having them registered. That's all I wanna hear."[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-154) When Hope shared these views during an [ABC Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_Radio "ABC News Radio") interview, he quickly realized the repercussions. Vice President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), who was visiting [West Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point "West Point") the same day Hope taped a special there, had declined to meet with him. Additionally, at a luncheon in Washington that same week, Hope had planned to sit with Nancy Reagan, but she canceled at the last minute.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-155)

Hope's views on the gay community also evolved. At the height of [Anita Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Bryant "Anita Bryant")'s campaign to reverse the progress of gay rights and anti-discrimination legislation in Florida in 1977, he, as well as many other comedians, ridiculed her in their routines, but also expressed his disagreement with Bryant: "We're all entitled to our own sexual habits [and] I believe what these people do behind closed doors is their business ... Most of us today are aware of Anita Bryant's stand [but] I still think jobs should be based on talent, not whether a person is homosexual or heterosexual."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-156) However, Texaco and Chrysler, sponsors for many of his TV specials, asked him to refrain from making further jokes about the subject.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-157) In February 1986, he joined [Elizabeth Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Taylor "Elizabeth Taylor"), to cohost a benefit for [American Foundation for AIDS Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Foundation_for_AIDS_Research "American Foundation for AIDS Research") and the [Arizona AIDS Fund Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_AIDS_Fund_Trust?action=edit&redlink=1 "Arizona AIDS Fund Trust (page does not exist)") in [Scottsdale, AZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsdale,_AZ "Scottsdale, AZ").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-158) Though expressing these supportive views, he occasionally used epithets and told jokes at the expense of the community yet showed remorse when called on it. During a performance at [Liberty Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Weekend "Liberty Weekend") in 1986, Hope remarked, "I just heard that the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty") has AIDS, but she doesn't know if she got it from the mouth of the [Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River") or the [Staten Island Ferry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_Ferry "Staten Island Ferry")."[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-159) Two months later, Hope took responsibility for telling the joke and apologized, explaining that he overheard the joke and thought it was funny.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-160) When Hope used the word "[fag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faggot "Faggot")" on a 1988 _[Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_ appearance, [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") asked for a statement apologizing for the slur. He agreed to tape a public service announcement opposing "bigotry" on their behalf.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-161)

### Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

Hope, who suffered from vision problems for much of his adult life, served as an active honorary chairman on the board of [Fight for Sight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight_for_Sight_(U.S.) "Fight for Sight (U.S.)"), a nonprofit organization in the United States which funds medical research in vision and ophthalmology. He hosted its _Lights On_ telecast in 1960 and donated $100,000 ($1.04M in 2024) to establish the Bob Hope Fight for Sight Fund.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Fight_for_Sight-162) Hope recruited numerous top celebrities for the annual "Lights On" fundraiser. As an example, he hosted boxing champion [Joe Frazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Frazier "Joe Frazier"), actress [Yvonne De Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvonne_De_Carlo "Yvonne De Carlo"), and singer-actor [Sergio Franchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi "Sergio Franchi") as headliners for the April 25, 1971, show at Philharmonic Hall in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee").[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Wilson_1971-163)

### Estate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Estate")]

Main article: [Hope Residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Residence "Hope Residence")

Hope settled into a home custom built for him in 1939 on an 87,000-square-foot (8,083 m 2) lot in the [Toluca Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake "Toluca Lake") section of [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California") in the [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley"). It was put on the market in late 2012.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMikailian2012-164)

The [Hope Residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Residence "Hope Residence") is a 23,366-square-foot (2,171 m 2)[modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernism "Modernism") home in [Palm Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs "Palm Springs"), built to resemble a volcano, that was designed in 1973 by [John Lautner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lautner "John Lautner"). The home is located above the city, with panoramic views of the [Coachella Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley "Coachella Valley") and the [San Jacinto Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jacinto_Mountains "San Jacinto Mountains"). It was put on the market for the first time in February 2013 with an asking price of $50 million,[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-NYTimes_February_2013-165) and sold to investor [Ron Burkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Burkle "Ron Burkle") for just $13 million in November 2016.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-166)

### Advanced age and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Advanced age and death")]

At the age of 93, seven years before his death, Hope converted to [Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholicism "Catholicism"), his wife's faith.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-seeing-stars_St_Charles-167)[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-168)

In July 1997 at age 94, he attended the funeral of [James Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Stewart "James Stewart"), where many pointed out his frail appearance.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-169) At the age of 95, Hope made an appearance at the 50th anniversary of the [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") with [Milton Berle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Berle "Milton Berle") and [Sid Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Caesar "Sid Caesar"). Contemporaries [Fay Wray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fay_Wray "Fay Wray") and [Gloria Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Stuart "Gloria Stuart") were also present.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Gallo_1998-170) Two years later, he was present at the opening of the Bob Hope Gallery of American Entertainment at the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress"). The Library of Congress has presented two major exhibitions about Hope's life: "Hope for America: Performers, Politics and Pop Culture" and "Bob Hope and American Variety".[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-myloc_hopeforamerica-171)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-loc_bobhope-172) He last made an appearance at the Hope Classic in 2000, where he hugged Swedish golfer [Jesper Parnevik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesper_Parnevik "Jesper Parnevik").[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-173)

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG/250px-Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG)

Graves of Bob and Dolores Hope, on the grounds of the Mission San Fernando Rey de España

In 1998, five years before his death, a prepared obituary written by [the Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Associated_Press "The Associated Press") was inadvertently released, resulting in Hope's death being announced on the floor of the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-c-span_June_1998-174)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998313-175) However, aside from increasing frailty, Hope remained in relatively good health until late in his old age.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002148-176) In June 2000 at age 97, he spent nearly a week in a California hospital being treated for [gastrointestinal bleeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_bleeding "Gastrointestinal bleeding").[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-CNN_June_2000-177) In August 2001 at age 98, he spent close to two weeks in a hospital recovering from [pneumonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumonia "Pneumonia").[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-178)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-guardian_September_2001-179)

Hope celebrated his 100th birthday on May 29, 2003.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-USA_Today_May_2003-180) To mark this event, the intersection of [Hollywood and Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_and_Vine "Hollywood and Vine") in Los Angeles was named "Bob Hope Square" and his centennial was declared "Bob Hope Day" in 35 states. Even at 100, Hope maintained his self-deprecating sense of humor, quipping, "I'm so old, they've canceled my [blood type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_type "Blood type")."[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-bbcdeath-181)

On July 27, 2003, Hope died of pneumonia at his home in [Toluca Lake, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake,_California "Toluca Lake, California").[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-bbcdeath-181) His grandson Zach Hope told [Soledad O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soledad_O'Brien "Soledad O'Brien") in an interview that, when asked at the end of his life where he wished to be buried, he said, "Surprise me".[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-CNN_July_29,_2003-182) His remains were temporarily placed in a mausoleum vault at the [San Fernando Mission Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Mission_Cemetery "San Fernando Mission Cemetery") before the construction of the Bob Hope Memorial Garden at the [San Fernando Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Mission "San Fernando Mission"), located next door to the cemetery, in Los Angeles. Dolores died in 2011, aged 102.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-183)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Doyle_2005-184) After his death, newspaper cartoonists worldwide paid tribute to his work for the USO, and some featured drawings of [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby"), who had died in 1977, welcoming Hope to Heaven.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-fac-assoc.org-185)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

**[Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope "Bob Hope")** (1903–2003) was a British-born American iconic entertainer.

**Bob Hope** may also refer to:

*   [Bob Hope (_Emmerdale_)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_(Emmerdale) "Bob Hope (Emmerdale)"), a character in _Emmerdale_, played by Tony Audenshaw
*   [MV _Bob Hope_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Bob_Hope "MV Bob Hope"), the lead vessel of the _Bob Hope_-class ships

The **1930s** (pronounced "nineteen-thirties"; shortened to the "**'30s**" and referred to as the "Thirties") was the [decade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decade "Decade") that began on January 1, 1930 and ended on December 31, 1939. In the United States, the [Dust Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_Bowl "Dust Bowl") led to the nickname the "Dirty Thirties".

The decade was defined by a global economic and political crisis that culminated in the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). It saw the collapse of the international financial system, beginning with the [Wall Street crash of 1929](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_Street_crash_of_1929 "Wall Street crash of 1929"), the largest [stock market crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_market_crash "Stock market crash") in American history. The subsequent economic downfall, called the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression"), had traumatic social effects worldwide, leading to widespread [poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty "Poverty") and [unemployment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment "Unemployment"), especially in the economic superpower of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weimar_Republic "Weimar Republic"), which was already struggling with the payment of reparations for the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"). The [Dust Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_Bowl "Dust Bowl") in the United States (which led to the nickname the "Dirty Thirties") exacerbated the scarcity of wealth. U.S. President [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt"), who took office in 1933, introduced a program of broad-scale social reforms and stimulus plans called the [New Deal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal "New Deal") in response to the crisis. The [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union")'s [second five-year plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five-year_plans_of_the_Soviet_Union#Second_plan,_1932%E2%80%931937 "Five-year plans of the Soviet Union") gave heavy industry top priority, putting the Soviet Union not far behind [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") as one of the major steel-producing countries of the world, while also improving communications. [First-wave feminism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-wave_feminism "First-wave feminism") made advances, with women gaining the right to vote in [South Africa (1930, whites only)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_Enfranchisement_Act,_1930 "Women's Enfranchisement Act, 1930"), [Brazil (1933)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminism_in_Brazil#20th_century "Feminism in Brazil"), and [Cuba (1933)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_Cuba#History "Women in Cuba"). Following the [rise of Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rise_of_Adolf_Hitler "Rise of Adolf Hitler") and the emergence of the [NSDAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSDAP "NSDAP") as the country's [sole legal party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_Against_the_Formation_of_Parties "Law Against the Formation of Parties") in 1933, Germany imposed [a series of laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuremberg_Laws "Nuremberg Laws") which discriminated against [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews") and other ethnic minorities.

Germany adopted an aggressive foreign policy, [remilitarizing the Rhineland (1936)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remilitarization_of_the_Rhineland "Remilitarization of the Rhineland"), annexing [Austria (1938)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anschluss "Anschluss") and the [Sudetenland (1938)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_Agreement "Munich Agreement"), before [invading Poland (1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Poland "Invasion of Poland") and starting [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") near the end of the decade. Italy likewise continued its already aggressive foreign policy, [defeating the Libyan resistance (1932)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Italo-Senussi_War "Second Italo-Senussi War") before [invading Ethiopia (1935)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Italo-Ethiopian_War "Second Italo-Ethiopian War") and then [Albania (1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_invasion_of_Albania "Italian invasion of Albania"). Both Germany and Italy [became involved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_response_to_the_Spanish_Civil_War#Support_for_Nationalists "International response to the Spanish Civil War") in the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War"), supporting the eventually victorious [Nationalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_faction_(Spanish_Civil_War) "Nationalist faction (Spanish Civil War)") led by [Francisco Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Franco "Francisco Franco") against the [Republicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_faction_(Spanish_Civil_War) "Republican faction (Spanish Civil War)"), who were in turn [supported by the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_response_to_the_Spanish_Civil_War#Soviet_Union "International response to the Spanish Civil War"). The [Chinese Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Civil_War "Chinese Civil War") was halted due to the need to confront Japanese imperial ambitions, with the [Kuomintang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuomintang "Kuomintang") and the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") forming a [Second United Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_United_Front "Second United Front") to fight Japan in the [Second Sino-Japanese War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War"). Lesser conflicts included interstate wars such as the [Colombia–Peru War (1932–1933)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia%E2%80%93Peru_War "Colombia–Peru War"), the [Chaco War (1932–1935)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaco_War "Chaco War") and the [Saudi–Yemeni War (1934)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi%E2%80%93Yemeni_War_(1934) "Saudi–Yemeni War (1934)"), as well as internal conflicts in [Brazil (1932)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitutionalist_Revolution "Constitutionalist Revolution"), [Ecuador (1932)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Civil_War_of_1932 "Ecuadorian Civil War of 1932"), [El Salvador (1932)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Matanza "La Matanza"), [Austria (1934)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Civil_War "Austrian Civil War") and [British Palestine (1936–1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936%E2%80%931939_Arab_revolt_in_Palestine "1936–1939 Arab revolt in Palestine").

[Severe famine took place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_famine_of_1930%E2%80%931933 "Soviet famine of 1930–1933") in the major grain-producing areas of the Soviet Union between 1930 and 1933, leading to 5.7 to 8.7 million deaths. Major contributing factors to the famine include: the forced [collectivization in the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collectivization_in_the_Soviet_Union "Collectivization in the Soviet Union") of agriculture as a part of the [First Five-Year Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_five-year_plan_(Soviet_Union) "First five-year plan (Soviet Union)"), forced grain procurement, combined with rapid industrialization, a decreasing agricultural workforce, and several severe droughts. A [famine of similar scope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_famines_in_China#Famines_in_China "List of famines in China") also took place in China from 1936 to 1937, killing 5 million people. The [1931 China floods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1931_China_floods "1931 China floods") caused 422,499–4,000,000 deaths. Major earthquakes of this decade include the [1935 Quetta earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935_Quetta_earthquake "1935 Quetta earthquake") (30,000–60,000 deaths) and the [1939 Erzincan earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1939_Erzincan_earthquake "1939 Erzincan earthquake") (32,700–32,968 deaths).

With the advent of [sound film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound_film "Sound film") in 1927, the musical—the genre best placed to showcase the new technology—took over as the most popular type of film with audiences, with the [animated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animated_film "Animated film")[musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_film "Musical film")[fantasy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_film "Fantasy film")_[Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow\_White\_and\_the\_Seven\_Dwarfs\_(1937\_film) "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937 film)")_ (1937) becoming the highest-grossing film of this decade in terms of gross rentals. In terms of distributor rentals, [_Gone with the Wind_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film) "Gone with the Wind (film)") (1939), an [epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_film "Epic film")[historical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama")[romance film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film"), was the highest-grossing film of this decade and remains the [highest-grossing film (when adjusted for inflation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_adjusted_for_inflation "List of highest-grossing films adjusted for inflation") to this day. Popularity of comedy films boomed after the [Silent era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_film "Silent film") with popular comedians [The Three Stooges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Three_Stooges "The Three Stooges") and [Marx Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marx_Brothers "Marx Brothers"). Popular novels of this decade include the [historical fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_fiction "Historical fiction") novels _[The Good Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good\_Earth "The Good Earth"),_ _[Anthony Adverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony\_Adverse\_(novel) "Anthony Adverse (novel)")_ and _[Gone with the Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone\_with\_the\_Wind\_(novel) "Gone with the Wind (novel)")_, all three of which were [best-selling novels in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers_Weekly_list_of_bestselling_novels_in_the_United_States_in_the_1930s "Publishers Weekly list of bestselling novels in the United States in the 1930s") for 2 consecutive years. [Cole Porter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Porter "Cole Porter") was a popular music artist in the 1930s, with two of his songs, "[Night and Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_and_Day_(song) "Night and Day (song)")" and "[Begin the Beguine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begin_the_Beguine "Begin the Beguine")" becoming No. 1 hits in 1932 and 1935 respectively. The latter song was of the [Swing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing_music "Swing music") genre, which had [begun to emerge as the most popular form of music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing_era "Swing era") in the United States since 1933.

The world population increased from 2.05 to 2.25 billion people during the decade, with about 750 million births and 550 million deaths.
